name: Valar Ventures

summary.text: Valar Ventures is a New York venture capital firm co-founded by Peter Thiel that specializes in providing startup capital to financial-services technology companies; its leadership includes Andrew McCormack and James Fitzgerald. In June 2025 The New York Times reported, from a confidential financial analysis of Jeffrey Epstein's estate, that Epstein put $40 million into two Valar funds in 2015 and 2016 and that the stake, then valued at nearly $170 million, was the largest asset still held by the estate. Thiel's spokesman has confirmed Epstein was a limited partner and denied that he co-owned the fund.

facts.claim: The New York Times reported in June 2025 that in 2015 and 2016 Epstein put $40 million into two funds managed by Valar Ventures, a New York firm co-founded by Peter Thiel, and that the investment was worth nearly $170 million according to a confidential financial analysis of Epstein's estate reviewed by the Times and a statement from a Valar spokesperson. The Times described the Valar stake as the largest asset still held by the estate.
facts.quote: In 2015 and 2016, Epstein put $40 million into two funds managed by Valar Ventures, a New York firm that was co-founded by Thiel. Today that investment is worth nearly $170 million, according to a confidential financial analysis of the late Epstein's estate reviewed by The New York Times and a statement provided by a Valar spokesperson.

facts.claim: Valar spokesperson Aaron Curtis said in a 2025 statement that when a firm representative met Epstein in 2014, Epstein was considered a 'well-known adviser to world leaders, top universities and philanthropic organizations.' Valar's leaders Andrew McCormack and James Fitzgerald said they hoped the eventual distribution of the investments 'can be put to positive use by helping victims move forward with their lives.' Thiel's spokesperson Jeremiah Hall declined to comment.
facts.quote: He said that when a firm representative met with Epstein in 2014, he was considered a "well-known adviser to world leaders, top universities and philanthropic organizations." Valar's leadership, Andrew McCormack and James Fitzgerald, said they hoped the eventual distribution of these investments can be put to positive use by helping victims move forward with their lives.

facts.claim: According to the Times' 2025 report, the estate's investment with Valar remained locked up and could not be paid out in cash. Victims who settled with the estate had signed broad releases giving up future claims against it, and the Times reported the proceeds were more likely to go to the estate's named beneficiaries, a former girlfriend and two long-term advisers of Epstein.
facts.quote: Those victims have already received monetary settlements from the estate, which required them to sign broad releases that gave up the right to bring future claims against it or individuals associated with it. Instead, the money is more likely to be distributed to one of Epstein's former girlfriends and two of his long-term advisers, who have been named the beneficiaries of his estate.

facts.claim: Byline Times reported in February 2026 that an email released in the Justice Department's Epstein files, written by former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak, described Thiel and Epstein as 'owners' of the fund. A spokesman for Thiel denied to Byline Times that Epstein was a co-owner of the fund with Thiel, but confirmed that Epstein was a limited partner.
facts.quote: a spokesman for Peter Thiel denied that Jeffrey Epstein was a co-owner of the fund with Thiel, but confirmed to Byline Times that he was a limited partner.

facts.claim: Byline Times reported in September 2025 that by June 2015 Epstein had committed $15 million through his Southern Trust Company as a limited partner in a Valar Ventures fund. This breakdown has not been reconciled with the $40 million total reported by The New York Times.
facts.quote: Epstein had committed a large sum, $15 million, through his Southern Trust Company as a limited partner in a key Valar Ventures fund by June 2015.

facts.claim: Epstein's released calendar and emails record a June 2014 dinner at which Thiel and former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak were present. The San Francisco Standard reported that Barak, according to emails he sent to friends, had dinner with the Palantir co-founder in June 2014 after agreeing to Epstein's overture.
facts.quote: Barak eventually agreed to Epstein's overture, and, according to emails he sent to friends, had dinner with the Palantir cofounder in June 2014.

sources.title: Inside the extended courtship linking Jeffrey Epstein, Peter Thiel, and Israeli officials

facts.claim: A 2023 Wall Street Journal review of Epstein's emails and schedules, as reported by the Daily Caller, found that Epstein scheduled at least six meetings with Thiel at his New York townhouse from 2014 to 2016 after Reid Hoffman's effort to connect the two. Thiel told the Journal: 'I was rather naive, and I didn't think enough about what Epstein's agenda might have been.' A Thiel spokesperson told The New York Times that Thiel 'never went to Epstein's Island.'
facts.quote: "I was rather naive," Thiel said, "and I didn't think enough about what Epstein's agenda might have been." ... Epstein scheduled at least six meetings with Thiel at his townhouse from 2014-16 following Hoffman's effort to connect Thiel to Epstein, according to the WSJ's review of Epstein's emails and schedules.

facts.claim: Daily calendars released by House Oversight Committee Democrats on September 26, 2025, from Epstein's estate, list a lunch scheduled with Thiel on November 27, 2017. Al Jazeera noted that the calendars do not indicate whether the scheduled meetings with Musk, Thiel and Bannon in fact took place, and that none of the three has been accused of wrongdoing related to Epstein.
facts.quote: The daily calendars do not indicate whether Epstein's meetings with Musk, Thiel and Bannon in fact took place. None of the three has been accused of wrongdoing related to Epstein.

facts.claim: Among the estate emails released by the House Oversight Committee in November 2025 is a November 2018 exchange in which Epstein wrote to Thiel, 'I liked your Trump exaggerations not lies,' and Thiel replied, 'Can't complain thus far.'
facts.quote: In a later exchange from November 2018, Epstein wrote to Thiel, "I liked your Trump exaggerations not lies." Thiel replied, "Can't complain thus far…"

facts.claim: CNBC reported in February 2026, from the Justice Department's Epstein file release, that Thiel began corresponding with Epstein as early as 2014, that the two exchanged emails coordinating in-person meetings several times a year at Epstein's New York home, Thiel's San Francisco office and Thiel's home, and that the exchanges continued into early 2019.
facts.quote: Thiel, who co-founded PayPal and Palantir, began corresponding with Epstein as early as 2014. The two exchanged emails coordinating in-person meetings several times per year at locations including Epstein's New York home, Thiel's San Francisco office and Thiel's home. Their exchanges continued into early 2019.

Reviewers of the records have said they do not indicate criminal wrongdoing by Thiel.
